pr_body:
Fixes #3290

## 😯 Current Behavior

Including a JS file from a html file (see test) (so the html is the parent of the JS) causes this test to fail (concat.js):
https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/41f106f3936b890d032f655f0fdb380d873352c5/packages/shared/scope-hoisting/src/concat.js#L83-L88

This works with only JS assets because some parent asset would include the `parcelRequire` prelude.

`Uncaught ReferenceError: parcelRequire is not defined`, because `parcelRequire.register()` is inserted (unnecessarily) and the `parcelRequire` isn't inserted.

## 💁 Possible Solution
`bundleGraph.isAssetReferenced(asset)` -> (imaginary) `bundleGraph.isAssetReferencedByJS(asset)`

issue_context.title: parcelRequire.register incorrectly added
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

If the entry HTML file has a single JS file as a script (and no dynamic imports) (like the react-hmr example), a `parcelRequire.register("...",{})` is inserted incorrectly (and this calls throws an error as well because the prelude defining `parcelRequire` wasn't inserted).

This is because `bundleGraph.isAssetReferenced(asset)` is true (referenced by the HTML file), but the module only needs to be registered if it's (dynamically) imported by a JS bundle. So the check should really be something like an imaginary `bundleGraph.isAssetReferencedByType(asset, "js")`.

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/baf40f7a331024bbfb3bb0394242fbd8d2928330/packages/shared/scope-hoisting/src/concat.js#L98-L103

```
Uncaught ReferenceError: parcelRequire is not defined:
	parcelRequire.register("1d046a184a4b101007cf746265aa38be",{})
```

CC @wbinnssmith I don't know if there's a way to get this information from the public bundleGraph?
comments:
> CC @wbinnssmith I don't know if there's a way to get this information from the public bundleGraph?

Currently not, but I like your proposal for `isAssetReferenced` with a type.

review_comments:
There was another issue in the function: it used`bundle.isEntry`, but it should really check: does `bundle` have any JS parent bundles (only the top level JS bundle should insert the prelude), not sure if this is the right way.

Thinking about this, what should happen if a HTML files has two JS script tags. Where should the prelude go? @devongovett
